learning_objective: 🎯 Bridge chemistry and biology! Explore the intricate chemical structures of the carbohydrates we eat, the proteins that build our muscles, and the DNA that holds our genetic code.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Ranging from simple sugars like glucose to complex polymers like starch and cellulose. Glucose has a 6-carbon open-chain structure, but in water, it folds into a stable 6-membered cyclic ring.
Proteins are long chain polymers made of amino acids joined together by 'Peptide Bonds'. Amino acids act as 'Zwitterions', meaning they have both a positive and negative charge on the same molecule!

Proteins have complex 3D shapes (primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary). When exposed to high heat or acid, the weak bonds holding the 3D shape break. The protein unfolds and loses its biological function, though its primary chain remains intact.

Essential organic compounds our bodies cannot synthesize. They are strictly classified as water-soluble (Vitamins B complex and C, which must be consumed daily) or fat-soluble (Vitamins A, D, E, and K, which are stored in the liver).
The blueprints of life. DNA is a double helix composed of nucleotides (a sugar + a phosphate + a nitrogenous base: A, T, G, C). RNA is single-stranded and uses Uracil (U) instead of Thymine (T).

fun_activity.title: 🥚 The Egg White Experiment
fun_activity.instructions: Crack an egg into a hot pan. The clear, runny egg white instantly turns into a solid, opaque white mass. This is exactly what 'Denaturation' looks like! The heat permanently unfolds the complex protein structures in the egg.

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize which vitamins are fat-soluble (A, D, E, K) and which are water-soluble (B, C). This is a guaranteed 1-mark question.
📌 Know the structural differences between DNA and RNA: DNA has Deoxyribose sugar and Thymine base. RNA has Ribose sugar and Uracil base.
📌 Be able to draw the Zwitterion structure of an amino acid. It perfectly explains their high melting points and solubility in water compared to normal organic amines/acids.
quick_recap: ⭐ Glucose and Fructose are both simple sugars, but glucose is an aldohexose (aldehyde group) while fructose is a ketohexose (ketone group).
⭐ 'Essential' amino acids must be obtained through your diet because the human body cannot synthesize them.
⭐ The two strands of DNA are complementary, not identical. Adenine (A) always pairs with Thymine (T) via 2 hydrogen bonds, and Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C) via 3 hydrogen bonds.
